c.tagline: Where Brazil began — the Discovery Coast's colonial cliff-top and endless Bahia beaches.

taxi.fareNote: City taxis are metered; agree a flat rate for longer resort or beach runs, and expect surcharges at night.

emergency.note: 190 reaches the military police, 192 the SAMU ambulance service, and 193 the fire brigade.

hood_landmark.Arraial d'Ajuda: Arraial d'Ajuda church cliff Porto Seguro

avoid.reason: Avoid the peripheral Baianão complex and other outlying favela districts, where most of the city's violent crime is concentrated.
Watch for pickpockets along the Passarela do Álcool and beach clubs, and avoid deserted stretches of beach after dark.

hood_desc: The Cidade Histórica perched on a high bluff over the ocean — a living museum of 16th-century colonial churches, the old jailhouse and grassy squares where Brazil's story began; best for history and sunset views.
The lively downtown seafront around the Passarela do Álcool, a nightly open-air strip of bars, craft stalls, capirinha vendors and street music; best for nightlife and dining.
Porto Seguro's prime beach strip north of town, lined with beach clubs, big resorts and calm reef-protected water; best for beach days and family resorts.
The northern coastal sprawl toward Coroa Vermelha, with reef pools, an indigenous craft market and the cross marking Brazil's first Mass; a quieter, spread-out resort area.
A bohemian beach village across the Buranhém River ferry, with a cliff-top church, Mucugê beach and the Broadway bar-and-restaurant strip; a laid-back but lively alternative base.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not reliably potable.

transit.hours: Municipal buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 11:00 PM; late-night trips rely on taxis and ride apps.
transit.note: Porto Seguro has no metro or rail; municipal buses, taxis, ride-hailing apps and the passenger/car ferry across the Buranhém River to Arraial d'Ajuda are the main ways to get around.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the onboard conductor; there is no rechargeable transit-card system.

bus: Intercity coaches to Salvador, Eunápolis and Vitória (Rodoviária de Porto Seguro)
ferry: Buranhém River car & passenger ferry to Arraial d'Ajuda

tip.r: A 10% service charge is usually added to restaurant bills; extra tipping is appreciated but not expected.
